title: Phase-zero failure-loop reachability
statement: Let $E\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each Boolean word, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,w\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $s\le w$. Let $i\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $i+1\le w$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be an 18-register machine state such that $n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,Q,E$ are all zero; $s$ and $w$ are its radius and width, respectively; $K=2^w$; $U,V<2^w$; $M\le2^w$; $I=i+1$; $SE<2^{w(w-(i+1))}$; and $SP<2^{w-(i+1)}$. If $M<2^w$ and $M_1\le2^w$, then there is a finite run from the phase-zero failure label with registers given by the state obtained from $\mathrm{st}$ by replacing $V$ with $M$, $M$ with $M_1$, and $E$ with the old value of $V$, to the loop label with registers given by the state obtained from $\mathrm{st}$ by replacing $M$ with $M+1$; every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies the guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle on four indices and Boolean words
Machine state $\mathrm{st}$ satisfies the stated zero-register, radius, width, code, level, and stack bounds
replaced:
Let $E\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle on four indices and Boolean words,
let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,w\in\mathbb N$ with $s\le w$. Let $i\in\mathbb N$
satisfy $i+1\le w$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a state satisfying the following
conditions: the registers $n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,Q,E$ are zero; the radius is $s$, the width is
$w$, and $K=2^w$; $U,V<2^w$, $M\le 2^w$, and $I=i+1$; and $SE<2^{w(w-(i+1))}$ and
$SP<2^{w-(i+1)}$. If $M<2^w$ and $M_1\le 2^w$, then from label $a0F$ with register
values $V=M$, $M=M_1$, and $E=V_{\mathrm{old}}$, the machine can reach label $loop$ with
the same state except that $M$ is increased by one. Every configuration before the
endpoint satisfies the guard with register bound $2^{w^2}$.
